events.title: Pope Celestine V resigns after five months
events.description: The hermit-pope Celestine V renounced the papacy, overwhelmed by its politics. Dante appears to condemn him for 'the great refusal', but the church later canonised him.
events.html: The hermit-pope Celestine V renounced the papacy, overwhelmed by its politics. Dante appears to condemn him for 'the great refusal', but the church later canonised him.

events.title: The Council of Trent opens
events.description: The Catholic Church's council opened at Trent in northern Italy and met, with long breaks, until 1563. It reaffirmed Catholic doctrine against Protestant teaching and reformed clerical discipline.
events.html: The Catholic Church's council opened at Trent in northern Italy and met, with long breaks, until 1563. It reaffirmed Catholic doctrine against Protestant teaching and reformed clerical discipline.

events.title: Abel Tasman sights New Zealand
events.description: Dutch navigator Abel Tasman sighted the west coast of New Zealand's South Island, the first recorded European sighting. A violent encounter with Māori in Golden Bay days later meant his crew never landed.
events.html: Dutch navigator Abel Tasman sighted the west coast of New Zealand's South Island, the first recorded European sighting. A violent encounter with Māori in Golden Bay days later meant his crew never landed.

events.title: Japanese troops capture Nanjing
events.description: Japanese forces took China's capital, Nanjing, and began weeks of mass killing, rape and looting. Estimates of the dead range from tens of thousands to over 300,000, and the massacre remains bitterly contested.

events.title: British cruisers fight the Graf Spee at the River Plate
events.description: Three British cruisers engaged the German pocket battleship Admiral Graf Spee off the River Plate estuary. Damaged, she took refuge in Montevideo, and four days later her captain scuttled her.
